1afcbcc315ae:
• 29 June: «The Holy Apostles Peter and Paul» – teachers of faith, repentance and the Church's mission in the world
• Happy name day to all who celebrate!
• In Orthodox iconography (and so also in the icon painted on glass in our workshop, which we are showing you today) the two apostles are painted together: Peter holding a bunch of keys and Paul a sword. What is the meaning of these two elements, what do these objects signify?
• Fr. Constantin Sturzu explains: «The keys that Saint Peter holds are “the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven”; they unlock the gates of Paradise, but only through the sacrament of repentance, or confession. The sword means the diligent preaching of the word of God: “For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart" (Hebrews 4:12). So if we receive the word of God, even if it stings at first like a cut from a sword, it then opens the gates of eternity to us, just as a key opens the door of a house»

3282d98aa1b8:
✤ 5 June 2023 – The Holy Trinity ✤
• Fr. Teofil Părăian: "We believe that God is One in being and threefold in person. It is a mystery of our faith, perhaps the greatest mystery, something we cannot understand but can receive through faith. This is the divine revelation."
• On the Monday after Pentecost Sunday (which is dedicated to glorifying the Holy Trinity), we are showing you the icon painted on glass in our workshop: «The Holy Trinity and the Coronation of the Mother of God» (model: workshop in Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century)
• The scene shows the Holy Trinity (the spiritual unity of the three divine persons): Jesus Christ carrying the Cross of the crucifixion, God the Father with the orb and sceptre (the insignia of the Almighty), and the Holy Spirit (as a white dove framed by the sun) sending down His blessing. The first two hold a crown above the head of the Virgin Mary (kneeling, dressed in a white maphorion, with her hands crossed on her chest). The figures are ”held up” by clouds
• This icon was made to order, so it is not available. If you would like a similar icon, contact me

f42e65222840:
✤ The Lamentation of Christ – icon on glass (57x62 cm), a study after an icon from the personal collection of Queen Marie (Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century)
✤ About the icon:
• The theme of this icon is the Lamentation of Jesus, after the Descent from the Cross and before the burial itself
• The icon is one of the rare compositions developed horizontally, as is proper to the epitaphios
• Its central scene shows the laying of Jesus Christ in the tomb: two apostles hold the shroud at His head and feet, and two angels lift Him from the front. In the background, Mary is surrounded by the holy women and by archangels; seraphim float in the air and (above the cross) the "thrones", angels set in medallions. In the corners of the scene the four Evangelists are shown in medallions. In the upper register, between the medallions and the arch of the vault, two landscapes can be seen: Mount Golgotha on the right and the city of Jerusalem on the left
• The technique is the traditional one: egg tempera and gold leaf
✤ The icon is not available
e90328968f1f:
• «Jesus with the Vine» – icon on glass (model: Șcheii Brașovului, early 19th century)
• This icon is also called “the Icon of the Eucharist”, a theme found only in Romanian iconography, especially in Transylvania
• The iconographic scene shows the risen Jesus Christ before the Cross (standing on the Holy Table of the Altar);
from His side grows a vine full of grapes, which Christ's hand presses straight into the Holy Chalice; from the image one can easily deduce that the icon does not aim to highlight the metaphor of the vine (frequent in the New Testament writings); it aims to highlight what we find in the Holy Chalice, namely: "in the form of the wine flowing from the grapes is the very Blood of Christ, for the vine grows and is nourished from His side, and on the Holy Table of the Altar lies the very body of the risen Christ"
• Would you like a similar icon? (this one is not available) Contact me and we will settle the details
4e3421178c74:
◘ «The Table of Paradise» or «The Heavenly Feast» – icon on glass (model: Nicula, 19th century)
◘ The iconographic theme divides the space of the composition into five rhombus-shaped fields, separated by bands decorated with the «rope» motif
◘ The central rhombus holds an oversized floral motif, which is repeated in the triangular fields next to the five rhombuses
◘ Leaning on the sides of the middle rhombus are the four rhombuses showing the guests taking part in the heavenly feast. The Mother of God with the Child and Jesus Christ blessing are always in the upper rhombuses; the others hold other saints, in this case Saint Paraskeva and Saint Nicholas the Hierarch
◘ This icon is not available. For a personalised order, you propose the saints you wish to have depicted in the two lower rhombuses
